S.FORM: ʔuuna=pa u-cani sua isi=mita kanakanavu.
S.PHON: ʔuunapa uʦani sua iʂimita kanakanavu
S.FORM: 'uunapa ucani sua isimita kanakanavu.
S.PHON: ʔuunapa uʦani sua iʂimita kanakanavu
S.TRANSL: We Kanakanavu people still have one taboo.

S.FORM: naatia=maku a-paica-ən sian pu-kari-kari.
S.PHON: naatiamaku apaiʦaən ʂian pukarikari
S.FORM: naatiamaku apaicaen sian pukarikari.
S.PHON: naatiamaku apaiʦaen ʂian puka[r|ɾ]ika[r|ɾ]i
S.TRANSL: I plan to talk about it by means of (the type recorder) here.

S.FORM: nakai ma-kaasi seŋsei=maku, "aa-paica-u=pa sian," pu-kari-kari misai.
S.PHON: nakai makaaʂi seŋseimaku aapaiʦaupa ʂian pukarikari misai
S.FORM: nakai makaasi sengseimaku, "aapaicaupa sian," pukarikari misai.
S.PHON: nakai makaaʂi seŋseimaku aapaiʦaupa ʂian puka[r|ɾ]ika[r|ɾ]i misai
S.TRANSL: But the professor said, "Please talk from here."

S.FORM: ʔuuna=pa u-cani isi=mita kanakanavu, vərəŋa.
S.PHON: ʔuunapa uʦani iʂimita kanakanavu vərəŋa
S.FORM: 'uunapa ucani isimita kanakanavu, verenga.
S.PHON: ʔuunapa uʦani iʂimita kanakanavu ve[r|ɾ]eŋa
S.TRANSL: We Kanakanavu people still have one taboo about eels.

S.FORM: sua kisa-i ma-maaraŋ, miana ma-kaasi ʔakun k<um>aən vərəŋa si puisia.
S.PHON: sua kisai mamaaraŋ miana makaaʂi ʔakun kumaən vərəŋa ʂi puiʂia
S.FORM: sua kisai mamaarang, miana makaasi 'akun k<um>aen verenga si puisia.
S.PHON: sua kisai mamaa[r|ɾ]aŋ miana makaaʂi ʔakun kumaen ve[r|ɾ]eŋa ʂi puiʂia
S.TRANSL: The elders in the past told us not to eat any eel because of the taboo.

S.FORM: u-cani maamia siu-ini.
S.PHON: uʦani maamia ʂiuini
S.FORM: ucani maamia siuini.
S.PHON: uʦani maamia ʂiuini
S.TRANSL: Each (eel) only has one intestine.

S.FORM: sua=kani vanai kaʔanə tia=k<um>a-kaən vərəŋa ia, k<um>aən=kita ia, siiu vərəŋa ni-mara-can-cani maamia
S.PHON: suakani vanai kaʔanə tiakumakaən vərəŋa ia kumaənkita ia ʂiiu vərəŋa nimaraʦanʦani maamia
S.FORM: suakani vanai ka'ane tiak<um>akaen verenga ia, k<um>aenkita ia, siiu verenga nimaracancani maamia
S.PHON: suakani vanai kaʔane tiakumakaen ve[r|ɾ]eŋa ia kumaenkita ia ʂiiu ve[r|ɾ]eŋa nima[r|ɾ]aʦanʦani maamia
S.TRANSL: The reason for not eating any eel is that the eel has only one intestine.

S.FORM: nai, cəʔəra-i vərəŋa puuʔa-an=ku=cu kauru sua tavaruŋa-ini araanai na əməca-ini. makaasi na taʔica-in ia, u-cani maamia siu-ini alaal-ai na taaʔiica-ini.
S.PHON: nai ʦəʔərai vərəŋa puuʔaankuʦu kauru sua tavaruŋaini araanai na əməʦaini makaaʂi na taʔiʦain ia uʦani maamia ʂiuini aɾaaɾai na taaʔiiʦaini
S.FORM: nai, ce'erai verenga puu'aankucu kauru sua tavarungaini araanai na emecaini. makaasi na ta'icain ia, ucani maamia siuini araarai na taa'iicaini.
S.PHON: nai ʦeʔe[r|ɾ]ai ve[r|ɾ]eŋa puuʔaankuʦu kau[r|ɾ]u sua tava[r|ɾ]uŋaini a[r|ɾ]aanai na emeʦaini makaaʂi na taʔiʦain ia uʦani maamia ʂiuini a[r|ɾ]aa[r|ɾ]ai na taaʔiiʦaini
S.TRANSL: Well, look at the eel that I bought, I cut it right down the middle from top to bottom, and there was only one intestine all the way.

S.FORM: iimu kisa-i ma-maaraŋ, miana ia, ʔakuni k<um>aən ʔinia si puisia.
S.PHON: iimu kisai mamaaraŋ miana ia ʔakuni kumaən ʔinia ʂi puiʂia
S.FORM: iimu kisai mamaarang, miana ia, 'akuni k<um>aen 'inia si puisia.
S.PHON: iimu kisai mamaa[r|ɾ]aŋ miana ia ʔakuni kumaen ʔinia ʂi puiʂia
S.TRANSL: So our elders in the old days said not to eat it because of a superstition.

S.FORM: tee=kani paa-taa-tanam vərəŋa. k<um>a-kaən=kia ala-sələcə na taaʔiica.
S.PHON: teekani paataatanam vərəŋa kumakaənkia aɾasəɾəʦə na taaʔiiʦa
S.FORM: teekani paataatanam verenga. k<um>akaenkia araserece na taa'iica.
S.PHON: teekani paataatanam ve[r|ɾ]eŋa kumakaenkia a[r|ɾ]ase[r|ɾ]eʦe na taaʔiiʦa
S.TRANSL: It is said that we would be like an eel: What we eat would come out of the buttocks just like an eel (= Our bowel movements will look like eels).

S.FORM: kisa-i ma-maaraŋ, miana ku-ʔupa-ʔupaŋ=kita k<um>aən ia, tee=kita makai vərəŋa kaən-ən maamia ala-sələcə, makai kisa-i sumukun.
S.PHON: kisai mamaaraŋ miana kuʔupaʔupaŋkita kumaən ia teekita makai vərəŋa kaənən maamia aɾasəɾəʦə makai kisai sumukun
S.FORM: kisai mamaarang, miana ku'upa'upangkita k<um>aen ia, teekita makai verenga kaenen maamia araserece, makai kisai sumukun.
S.PHON: kisai mamaa[r|ɾ]aŋ miana kuʔupaʔupaŋkita kumaen ia teekita makai ve[r|ɾ]eŋa kaenen maamia a[r|ɾ]ase[r|ɾ]eʦe makai kisai sumukun
S.TRANSL: Our elders in the old days said that we would be like an eel: What we eat haphazardly would come out of the buttocks just like an eel. It is also said like the Bunun.

S.FORM: k<um>a-kaən ala-sələcə sua iikita kanakanavu ia, k<um>a-kaən ala-sələcə, ala-sələcə maamia naa taaʔiica sua ni-kaən-a mu-a-lavu=ci=kia.
S.PHON: kumakaən aɾasəɾəʦə sua iikita kanakanavu ia kumakaən aɾasəɾəʦə aɾasəɾəʦə maamia naa taaʔiiʦa sua nikaəna muaɾavutʂikia
S.FORM: k<um>akaen araserece sua iikita kanakanavu ia, k<um>akaen araserece, araserece maamia naa taa'iica sua nikaena muaravucikia.
S.PHON: kumakaen a[r|ɾ]ase[r|ɾ]eʦe sua iikita kanakanavu ia kumakaen a[r|ɾ]ase[r|ɾ]eʦe a[r|ɾ]ase[r|ɾ]eʦe maamia naa taaʔiiʦa sua nikaena mua[r|ɾ]avutʂikia
S.TRANSL: We Kanakanavu people believed that what we had eaten would come out of the buttocks, and we would get hungry just like an eel.

S.FORM: makasua sua vərəŋa. naatia=ku=kan, puutu-cu-culu.
S.PHON: makasua sua vərəŋa naatiakukan puutuʦuʦuɾu
S.FORM: makasua sua verenga. naatiakukan, puutucucuru.
S.PHON: makasua sua ve[r|ɾ]eŋa naatiakukan puutuʦuʦu[r|ɾ]u
S.TRANSL: That is how it is with an eel. I took this to be true.

S.FORM: cu-culu sua kisa-i ma-maaraŋ miana ia, kaʔan pə-rəsəvə, si cu-cculu uu-pia-ni=ci ni-para-pici=maku vərəŋa miana.
S.PHON: ʦuʦuɾu sua kisai mamaaraŋ miana ia kaʔan pərəsəvə ʂi ʦuʦʦuɾu uupianitʂi niparapitʂimaku vərəŋa miana
S.FORM: cucuru sua kisai mamaarang miana ia, ka'an pereseve, si cuccuru uupianici niparapicimaku verenga miana.
S.PHON: ʦuʦu[r|ɾ]u sua kisai mamaa[r|ɾ]aŋ miana ia kaʔan pe[r|ɾ]eseve ʂi ʦuʦʦu[r|ɾ]u uupianitʂi nipa[r|ɾ]apitʂimaku ve[r|ɾ]eŋa miana
S.TRANSL: Ancient people in the past told the truth, and they did not tell a lie because I bisected several eels to find that out.

S.FORM: kuu=pi=kia m-ara-pici, cu-cculu u-cani maamia siu-ini.
S.PHON: kuupikia marapitʂi ʦuʦʦuɾu uʦani maamia ʂiuini
S.FORM: kuupikia marapici, cuccuru ucani maamia siuini.
S.PHON: kuupikia ma[r|ɾ]apitʂi ʦuʦʦu[r|ɾ]u uʦani maamia ʂiuini
S.TRANSL: I did not know the truth that (an eel) had only one intestine before I bisected it.

S.FORM: ʔakia sua ni-ma-caʔa na ʔuna-ini. ni-ma-caʔa sua siu-ini ia, ma-naasə naatia=pa ʔuuna taa-usukain-a ni-kaən=kiai.
S.PHON: ʔakia sua nimaʦaʔa na ʔunaini nimaʦaʔa sua ʂiuini ia manaasə naatiapa ʔuuna taausukaina nikaənkiai
S.FORM: 'akia sua nimaca'a na 'unaini. nimaca'a sua siuini ia, manaase naatiapa 'uuna taausukaina nikaenkiai.
S.PHON: ʔakia sua nimaʦaʔa na ʔunaini nimaʦaʔa sua ʂiuini ia manaase naatiapa ʔuuna taausukaina nikaenkiai
S.TRANSL: There are no sections in an intestine. What we have eaten will certainly get stuck somewhere.

S.FORM: u-cani maamia ma-kaasi na taʔica-ini.
S.PHON: uʦani maamia makaaʂi na taʔiʦaini
S.FORM: ucani maamia makaasi na ta'icaini.
S.PHON: uʦani maamia makaaʂi na taʔiʦaini
S.TRANSL: It has only one intestine running from head to tail.

S.FORM: kaən-ən=kiai maamia mu-nalusu m-utaʔi.
S.PHON: kaənənkiai maamia munaɾusu mutaʔi
S.FORM: kaenenkiai maamia munarusu muta'i.
S.PHON: kaenenkiai maamia muna[r|ɾ]usu mutaʔi
S.TRANSL: So once it eats something, it passes through its body very quickly.

S.FORM: iikita=kani si kanakanavu miana ia, maka-sua=kani, u-cani maamia siu-in sua misai. ma-maaraŋ miana.
S.PHON: iikitakani ʂi kanakanavu miana ia makasuakani uʦani maamia ʂiuin sua misai mamaaraŋ miana
S.FORM: iikitakani si kanakanavu miana ia, makasuakani, ucani maamia siuin sua misai. mamaarang miana.
S.PHON: iikitakani ʂi kanakanavu miana ia makasuakani uʦani maamia ʂiuin sua misai mamaa[r|ɾ]aŋ miana
S.TRANSL: Our elders in the past said each (eel) has only one intestine.

S.FORM: vanai=kita kanakanavu kaʔan taavalaʔə=ta, ʔupa-ʔupaŋ ma-maaraŋ miana makaasua.
S.PHON: vanaikita kanakanavu kaʔan taavaɾaʔəta ʔupaʔupaŋ mamaaraŋ miana makaasua
S.FORM: vanaikita kanakanavu ka'an taavara'eta, 'upa'upang mamaarang miana makaasua.
S.PHON: vanaikita kanakanavu kaʔan taava[r|ɾ]aʔeta ʔupaʔupaŋ mamaa[r|ɾ]aŋ miana makaasua
S.TRANSL: For this reason, we Kanakanavu people cannot do things haphazardly, as our elders (said) in the past.
